text:
**What it is:** Sequence is an architecture scanning tool that reads a repository into a live, verifiable graph of its services, modules, and connections.

**Who it is for:** Newcomers and developers who want to understand how their software components interact — without relying on static documentation.

**Why it exists:** As code changes, the architecture can drift from what the manifest says. Sequence keeps the architecture honest by scanning real imports, calls, routes, and manifests in the codebase.

**How it works:**
1. Sequence runs static analysis on your repository to build an architecture graph.
2. The graph visualizes real service, module, and file connections drawn from code.
3. It attaches this graph to the chat so queries can be answered from it.
4. Only edges with real evidence appear solid; proposed or drawn edges remain dashed until found.
5. The whole thing runs on your machine with Node.js and pnpm — no cloud required.

**Advantages:** It gives you a real-time, code-verified view of your architecture instead of trusting static files or assumptions.
